one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on Oct 28, before the open, with the call at 1pm ET. Guidance is $9.3-9.4B in sales and $0.70-0.71 split-adjusted adj EPS. Amphenol has a long record of beating its own guide and raising, and Q2 orders ($10.7B, book-to-bill 1.23) plus a CommScope raise point to another beat with a Q4 guide above consensus. That is mostly expected, though, and the stock is near the top of its 52-week range ($89.26 high), so the reaction is close to symmetric with a small positive tilt. Hyperscaler Q3 capex prints in late October (MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN) also fall in the window. Every one raised or held guidance last round, so the cut risk looks low. I set the median at ~$86.6 (+1%) with monthly sigma ~13.5% (46%/3.5 plus a little extra for earnings).

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS $3.65 x 24x = $87.6. 40% FCF yield: forward FCF/share $3.40 / 3.75% = $90.7. Blend ~$88.8.

bear.story: AI capex digests in 2027-28. Goldman already models capex growth falling to ~12% in 2028, and hyperscaler FCF is strained (only 1 of 6 is forecast FCF-positive in 2027). IT datacom (43% of sales) stops growing, book-to-bill drops below 1, and the multiple falls to ~18x on ~$3.10 EPS.

base.story: 2027 roughly in line with consensus: revenue ~$42B, EPS ~$3.3, margins ~29%, CommScope optics adds to growth. The multiple compresses from 29x to ~24x NTM as growth slows to the teens, so the price ends near today's level plus EPS growth.

bull.story: 2027 capex lands at or above the $1.2-1.45T Goldman/UBS forecasts and 2028 keeps growing. CPO and power interconnect raise content per rack, EPS beats reach $4.2+ for the year ahead, and the market holds ~28x.

thesis_break_reason: $62 is about 28% below spot, back to the 52-week low area ($59) and below 19x 2027 consensus EPS. At that level the market would be pricing an AI interconnect order downturn (book-to-bill below 1, IT datacom decelerating sharply) or a hyperscaler capex cut, not ordinary volatility. A community analyst's sell signal (book-to-bill below 1.0 for two quarters) is the fundamental marker to watch.

reasoning: Facts: APH split 2:1 on 2026-09-03, so all per-share figures are split-adjusted. Q2 2026 sales were $8.8B (+55%, +30% organic), adj EPS $0.675, orders $10.7B (book-to-bill 1.23). IT datacom is 43% of sales and grew 63% organically. Q3 guide: $9.3-9.4B sales, $0.70-0.71 EPS. Net debt is $14.1B and diluted shares ~2.58B. Alternative-lane signals were constructive on demand but split on price. (1) The Supercycle capex tracker shows all 7 AI spenders raised or held 2026 guidance, with $214B spent last quarter. (2) Revelio job-posting data has active postings up ~27% YoY while headcount is flat, a sign of hiring ahead of capacity. (3) Polymarket 'AI bubble burst by Dec 31 2026' is at 8% ($2.4M volume) and by Jun 30 2027 at 18% (thin, ~$9k volume), checked 2026-10-02. (4) Independent writers disagree: the Oakridge Substack puts intrinsic value at ~$54 and calls the stock overvalued at 25x forward, while a Simply Wall St community narrative puts it at ~$104. Sell-side consensus is ~$99. My valuation is about $89, roughly at spot: EPS growth of ~11-19% is mostly offset by multiple compression from 29x to ~24x NTM as capex growth decelerates (Goldman: +54% in 2027, +12% in 2028). For the distribution I used a mixture: 80% lognormal with median $92 and sigma 0.36 (base/bull), plus 20% bear lognormal with median $62 and sigma 0.40 (capex digestion). The overall median is ~$86 and the mean ~$91, with spread a bit under the 46% realized vol, which was inflated by the AI-cycle and split-period swings. Limits: Reddit's API was blocked (HTTP 403 page) and X posts were not reachable, so social sentiment comes from newsletters and community sites. Twelve Data fundamentals and estimates endpoints were paywalled. I did not look up any option data.
